title: Mathematical and circuit prerequisites
diagnostic: Derive the current of an RL step and identify its state variable.
Identify poles and zeros from a rational transfer function and sketch asymptotic Bode slopes.
Convert amplitude ratios to dB and distinguish average, RMS, and peak-to-peak.
Perform one explicit-Euler step and explain local truncation error.

lessons.title: State variables and constitutive laws
lessons.physicalIntuition: Inductor current and capacitor voltage carry memory. Resistors dissipate energy but do not add an independent energy state.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Use vL = L di/dt and iC = C dv/dt with a declared passive sign convention. Integrate over a finite interval and check dimensions. Define average, RMS, and peak-to-peak as different functionals of a waveform.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The minimum buck state is one current per phase plus a shared capacitor voltage. Terminal output voltage may also include algebraic ESR/ESL terms and must not silently replace the capacitor state.
assumptions: lumped linear L and C unless otherwise stated
lessons.transferQuestion: If capacitor ESR is added, which quantity remains a dynamic state and which becomes an algebraic terminal-voltage term?

lessons.title: Laplace, poles, zeros, and Bode plots
lessons.physicalIntuition: A pole marks stored energy that cannot follow arbitrarily fast; a zero marks a signal path that changes the response numerator. Phase records timing/energy lag in sinusoidal steady state, not a hardware phase branch.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Transform linear differential equations with stated initial conditions, factor numerator and denominator, and derive asymptotic magnitude/phase contributions. Use 20 log10 for amplitude ratios and 10 log10 for power ratios.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Every plotted transfer function must name input, output, operating point, linearization, units, and phase convention. Numerical pole placement must match the implemented circuit/topology.
lessons.transferQuestion: What changes in the Bode plot if a zero moves from one decade below to one decade above a double pole?

lessons.title: Feedback algebra and numerical integration
lessons.physicalIntuition: Feedback reuses measured error to oppose disturbance; numerical integration approximates continuous state change with finite steps and can miss an event inside a step.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Derive y/r = G/(1+GH) for the declared negative-feedback signs. Compare explicit Euler x[n+1] = x[n] + h f[n] with trapezoidal integration and show why an unlocated discontinuity breaks smooth-step error assumptions.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The engine must split or locate switching events, warn when h is coarse relative to pulse width/delay, and never equate a smaller h with physical validation.
assumptions: feedback blocks are compatible and linear for the algebra
integration formulas apply piecewise between events
lessons.transferQuestion: Why can two Euler runs appear converged while both use the wrong switch-state equation?
